Finding B1 of the second DDD pass (#139). Severity: medium.

`commands.CATALOGUE`'s own comment claims "a Command the game can build and a Command the daemon accepts cannot drift apart" (`src/cti_daemon/commands.py:37–38`), but the daemon's own validation never reads the catalogue:

- `port.HANDLERS` (`src/cti_daemon/port.py:464`) restates the verb set as its keys.
- Each handler restates its Command's required args by hand (`command.args.get("squad_type")` at `port.py:217`, `args.get("squad")` at `port.py:288` and `port.py:361`, `args.get("order")`/`args.get("place")` at `port.py:354,369`).
- The five Effects actually pushed (`campaign.py:246,290,328,516`, `report_cycle.py:277`) are held to `commands.EFFECTS`'s declared args only by hand; `parse_effect` validates envelope shape, not the catalogue.

So the schema source is single for the SQF side (the export is tested, `tests/unit/test_export_command_schema.py`) and duplicated inside the daemon. A verb or argument changed on one side of that duplication is caught by nothing in `just unit` — the drift lands as an in-world discovery, which is the exact failure mode #74 removed on the inbound path.

Acceptance criteria:

- [ ] A unit test asserts `set(port.HANDLERS) == set(commands.CATALOGUE)`.
- [ ] A unit test (or property test) asserts that each pushed Effect's args exactly match `commands.EFFECTS[name]` — either by testing the producers, or by an assertion at `Outbox.push`/`Effect` construction that a test exercises; state which and why.
- [ ] The handlers' required-arg reads are either derived from `CATALOGUE` or coupled to it by a test, so an argument added to the catalogue without a handler reading it (or vice versa) is a red `just unit`.
- [ ] No wire format change; `just fast` green.
